chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah

Al-Jareeri, the brother of Ishaq, says to us: 'You say that there are two calls (from heaven), so which of them is the truthful one and which is the false one?' Abu Abdillah said: 'Say to him: He who informed us of that, while you deny that this will happen, is the truthful one.'

key_terms.الجريري: Al-Jareeri (a specific narrator or scholar known as the brother of Ishaq)
key_terms.نداءان: Two calls (referring to the two divine announcements before the appearance of the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: How do we distinguish between the two heavenly calls according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) addresses the epistemological challenge of verifying eschatological signs amidst human skepticism. He employs a pragmatic argument of authority, asserting that the truth of the 'two calls' (al-Nida'an) rests on the reliability of the divine messenger who reported them, regardless of whether the observer doubts the event's occurrence. This highlights the Shia principle of relying on the Imam's testimony for knowledge of the unseen (al-Ghayb) that transcends immediate empirical verification.
